reasoning: The corn ear displays the hallmark blue-green to teal colored powdery/granular fungal growth concentrated between kernel rows and at kernel bases, with yellow-orange kernels still visible beneath. This distinctive blue-green coloration concentrated in the inter-kernel spaces creating a banded appearance is the diagnostic visual hallmark of Trichoderma ear rot, clearly distinguishing it from the olive-green of Aspergillus, white cottony growth of Diplodia, or pink coloration of Gibberella/Fusarium.
